clue.text: Divine fellows in Scripture a bit spare

indicators.note: in tells us the divines and fellows sit inside the abbreviation for Scripture

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first part of Scripture
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the usual crossword shorthand for a divine or clergyman
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Learned clergymen poring over the Bible in their spare moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective but is a noun here, a churchman with the letters DD after his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap, a bit spare after the rest is used, is called an oddment.

clue.text: Ring to get set of books containing firm's expenses

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: containing means the books abbreviation holds the firm inside it

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books
Co is company, a firm; firm's gives the possessive S

explanation.surface: A phone call to the bookkeeper about the company's costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oncosts are overheads, expenses of running a business not tied to one product; the plural matches.

clue.text: What is evident in messy sort of game

parts.note: what stands out in the word messy is a doubled letter, a repeat side by side

indicators.note: in points to a letter within messy, the one that appears twice in a row

explanation.surface: Something obvious about a chaotic kind of match.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'What is evident in messy' reads as 'double S', the pair of S letters in messy; the parse splits it as DOUBLE plus that letter. Doubles is tennis or badminton played two a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubles is a form of tennis and other racket games played in pairs.

clue.text: Treasury no longer wants one method of payment, right?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
paying by cheque is a method of payment

explanation.surface: The Treasury is said to be phasing out cheques.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to banks phasing out cheques; 'wants' is a link here. The Exchequer is the UK government's treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the British government department in charge of public revenue, the national treasury.

clue.text: Garment of past time turning up here

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Clothing from a bygone age reappears here.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator turns the whole run TAGO, giving the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A toga is the loose outer garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Boy in agony makes one peer

indicators.note: in places the young male inside the word for agony

parts.note: agony is pain
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A suffering youngster somehow turns out to be a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The paladins were the twelve peers of Charlemagne's court, so one of them is one peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paladins were the legendary twelve peers attending Charlemagne, so a single knight of that band is one peer.

clue.text: Two or three perhaps opposing friend at the very beginning

parts.note: two and three are both prime numbers
V for versus means opposing
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A couple of people perhaps set against a friend from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval means belonging to the earliest ages, so the adverb describes something at the very beginning.

clue.text: Person of authority, but not serious

explanation.definitionFit: A leading figure is called a light, and light also means frivolous.

clue.text: Editor upset more delicate creator of Times Two clues?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: finer means more delicate

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is upset about a more refined puzzle setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Times Two is The Times' quick crossword, whose clues are plain definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue that is just a definition is set by someone who defines, so the Quick Crossword setter is a definer.

clue.text: No methods for securing advantage in the current period?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the methods enclose the advantage

parts.note: ways are methods
AD is short for advantage in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: No current means of locking in an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means at the present time, these days.

clue.text: Having a liking for hymns? Chap with this may produce a piano

parts.words: Chap with this may produce a piano
parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: when CH, short for church, goes from the word chap, AP is left, which is A plus P for piano

explanation.surface: A hymn-loving man somehow conjures up a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a standard abbreviation for church and P (piano, soft) is the musical marking; the definition is loose, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who regularly attends services may be assumed to enjoy hymns, a playful gloss on habitual worship.

clue.text: Hardly any expression of relief audible

indicators.note: audible says we want what the exclamation sounds like when spoken

parts.note: phew is what people say when relieved

explanation.surface: Barely anyone sighs with relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Few means a small number, scarcely any at all.

clue.text: One preserving so wants change for nothing

indicators.note: wants ... for means lacks one thing and has another in its place, so the O of so is swapped out

parts.note: O is the round zero, nothing
to change is to alter

explanation.surface: Someone who preserves things wants a change for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the word 'so', remove its O (nothing) and put ALTER (change) in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A salter cures meat or fish with salt, a way of preserving food.

clue.text: Designated two little chaps to collect money

indicators.note: to collect means the two chaps gather the money between them

parts.note: Des is a short form of Desmond
Ed is a short form of Edward
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A pair of small boys are appointed to take the collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something destined has been set aside or marked out in advance, that is, designated.

clue.text: Conservative woman hoards lots, ungenerous person

indicators.note: hoards means keeps inside, so the woman's run holds the lots

parts.note: Kate is a woman's name
heaps means lots

explanation.surface: A Tory lady stockpiles loads and gives nothing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who avoids spending money.

clue.text: Person protecting the plant against end of January wind

indicators.note: against means placed next to
protecting means wrapping around, so the person encloses the plant

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'
an aster is a daisy-like flower

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of January

explanation.surface: A gardener shields a plant from the bitter wind at the end of January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' just sets Y beside the rest; the definition is the single word at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A southeasterly is a wind blowing from the southeast.

clue.text: End of story sweetness and light, we've heard

indicators.note: we've heard says the pieces are taken by their spoken form

parts.note: a tale is a story; sweetness and light is harmony, peace

explanation.surface: A tale ending on a note of harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of story' looks like the definition; only 'End' defines, with 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a final part, as an ornament at the end of a chapter.

clue.text: Famous man behind bars, suffering in the Scrubs endlessly

indicators.note: suffering signals the letters being knocked about into a new order
endlessly takes off the final letter of Scrubs

explanation.surface: A notorious man in jail, having a bad time in Wormwood Scrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' suggests prison, Wormwood Scrubs being a London jail, but the composer stands behind bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated composer is responsible for, or behind, the bars of music he wrote.

clue.text: Grouse, having to prepare' special article without payment at the end

indicators.note: to prepare signals the letters of special article being made ready in a new order
without means leaving a letter out of the fodder
at the end picks the final letter of payment

explanation.surface: Bird-shooting grouse made into a special item for free.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T (end of payment) from SPECIALARTICLE and rearrange the remaining thirteen letters. 'Grouse' looks like a complaint; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The capercaillie is the largest kind of grouse, a woodland game bird of Scotland.

clue.text: Plant put in a vase finally for arranging

indicators.note: for arranging asks for the letters to be arranged like flowers
finally takes the last letter of vase

explanation.surface: Instructions to place a flower in a vase for a display.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Actress continues to glide gracefully

parts.note: to swan is to move with graceful ease
on as in carries on, continues

explanation.surface: A star goes on gliding elegantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Swanson starred in Sunset Boulevard (1950).
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood film star of the silent and early sound eras.

clue.text: Fake sweetheart, soft initially

indicators.note: initially puts the soft letter at the start

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
honey is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: A false lover, gentle at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney means fake or not genuine.

clue.text: Increase confidence around hospital — it makes for buoyancy

parts.note: to up is to increase

indicators.note: around means the confidence word encloses the hospital letter

parts.note: trust is confidence
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Boosting morale at a hospital keeps patients afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Upthrust is the upward force a fluid exerts on a body, which is what keeps it buoyant.

clue.text: Horse going the wrong way will get run over

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards

parts.note: a pacer is a harness-racing horse

explanation.surface: A horse running the wrong way will be hit by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run over' suggests a road accident; it means to go over again, summarise.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or go back over points, as in running over them.

clue.text: Extravagant display cut, pence being limited

indicators.note: being limited means held inside, so pence is enclosed by the cut

parts.note: a slash is a cut

explanation.surface: A lavish show is trimmed because money is short.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to put on a showy, extravagant display.

clue.text: Move with difficulty as monster missing leg

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the leg letters come out

parts.note: a dragon is a monster
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A creature with one leg gone struggles along.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag oneself is to move slowly and with effort.

clue.text: When there may be poetic red sky observed (sun's beginning to go)

definitions.text: When there may be poetic red sky

indicators.note: to go says a letter is to be removed from the word for observed

parts.note: seen means observed

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of sun

explanation.surface: A red sky is seen as the sun starts to go down.
explanation.walkthrough: E'EN is the poetic contraction of evening, the time for 'red sky at night'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic contraction of evening names sunset time, when a red sky may be seen.

clue.text: It could be senior chap, gender ultimately being uncertain

definitions.text: It could be senior chap, gender ultimately being uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain says the letters are unsettled and must be rearranged
ultimately picks the last letter of gender

explanation.surface: A senior figure might be a man, but the gender is not fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The gender-neutral title is exactly what you use when the sex of the person at the top is unspecified, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairperson is the head of a meeting or board, a title chosen to leave the holder's sex unspecified.

clue.text: Ambushes to ensnare one before end of the walk

indicators.note: before puts the trapped part ahead of the final letter
to ensnare means the traps catch and hold the numeral inside them

parts.note: traps are ambushes
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the

explanation.surface: Lying in wait for a walker near the end of the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or aimlessly.

clue.text: Insect female disposed of in ecofriendly way

indicators.note: disposed of means got rid of, so the female letter is removed

parts.note: a greenfly is an aphid

explanation.surface: An eco-minded gardener gets rid of aphids without harming the environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means environmentally friendly, so the adverb describes acting in that manner.
